overview:
Alabama's 1st District is an open seat after redistricting, and it leans strongly Republican with a partisan advantage of about 17 points. Jerry Carl, the Republican, holds an overwhelming financial edge, having raised more than $1.1 million and benefiting from roughly $550,000 in outside spending, while Democrat Clyde Jones Jr. has raised under $100,000. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race.

Prediction markets give the Republican about a 95% chance of winning, in line with the district's fundamentals. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican victory in the mid-to-high teens, with modest uncertainty given the absence of polling.
